import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_50/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_50/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_50/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_50/training_3.csv", index_col=0)
source4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_50/training_4.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source5_50_4 with Source5_50_0 on Ship_id
df = pd.merge(source4, source0, on="Ship_id", how="inner")

# Join the result with Source5_50_1 on Ord_id
df = pd.merge(df, source1, on="Ord_id", how="inner")

# Join the result with Source5_50_2 on Prod_id
df = pd.merge(df, source2, on="Prod_id", how="inner")

# Join the result with Source5_50_3 on Cust_id
df = pd.merge(df, source3, on="Cust_id", how="inner")

# Group by Ship_Date (primary key) to ensure uniqueness and match target keys
df = df.groupby("Ship_Date", as_index=False).first()

# Select only the target columns with correct types and names
# Target schema: ['Ship_Date': string, 'Ord_id': integer, 'Prod_id': integer, 'Ship_id': integer]
# Convert Ord_id, Prod_id, Ship_id to integer by extracting numeric part after underscore
df["Ord_id"] = df["Ord_id"].str.extract(r'(\d+)').astype(int)
df["Prod_id"] = df["Prod_id"].str.extract(r'(\d+)').astype(int)
df["Ship_id"] = df["Ship_id"].str.extract(r'(\d+)').astype(int)

# Keep Ship_Date as string (already string)
result = df[["Ship_Date", "Ord_id", "Prod_id", "Ship_id"]]

# Write to output CSV
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_50/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
